issue_paraphrase: Declaring an option with is_flag=False together with an explicit flag_value and a default, then passing the option name with no value (for example --name), makes click refuse the argument with 'Option --name requires an argument' and exit code 2. Such an option should behave like a valueless flag: when the flag is given by itself it should use the flag_value and succeed, while an explicit value should still be accepted when one is supplied.
fix_summary: In Option.__init__, for non-flag options the internal _flag_needs_value flag is now computed as `flag_value is not UNSET or self.default is UNSET` instead of `self.default is UNSET`. With an explicit flag_value the parser is told the value is omittable, so at parse time _get_value_from_state returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE and process_value falls back to the flag_value, while an explicitly supplied value is still consumed.
notes: No network needed at test time. Both directions plus golden test take ~0.2s at 1 CPU. Do not use a bare grep for 'flag_value is not UNSET' as proof of the fix: that phrase already appears 4 times in parent core.py; the discriminating line is the `_flag_needs_value` assignment itself. pyproject.toml sets testpaths=tests, addopts="-m not stress", filterwarnings=error; running a single nodeid works.

issue_paraphrase: When a FuncParamType conversion function raises ValueError with its own message, click throws that message away and reports only the raw input string in the resulting BadParameter error. A meaningful validation message such as 'bad value: nope' never reaches the user; they see the offending value echoed back instead. The ValueError's message should be the one shown, falling back to the old input-echoing behavior only when the exception message is empty.
fix_summary: FuncParamType.convert now catches ValueError as exc, captures str(exc) as the message, and calls self.fail(message, ...) with it (falling back to str(value) only when the message is empty, still handling UnicodeError). Previously it always failed with str(value), losing the exception's message. (Commit message cites PR #3211; the changelog attributes it to issue #3105.)
notes: No network needed at test time. Both directions plus golden test take ~0.05s at 1 CPU. The golden test is parametrized with 2 cases; at the parent only the non-empty-message case fails, which still makes the test fail overall; at the fix both pass. pyproject.toml sets filterwarnings=error but nothing in this path triggers a warning.

issue_paraphrase: Running a command or group that has no arguments to parse but is set to show its help text when invoked with no arguments (no_args_is_help, which defaults to on for groups) exits with status 0, exactly like a successful run. Callers and scripts have no way to detect that only help was shown. Help displayed in this situation should end with the same non-zero exit status (2) as other usage errors, instead of success.
fix_summary: Command.parse_args and Group.parse_args now raise a new NoArgsIsHelpError (a UsageError, so it exits with code 2) instead of echoing the help text and calling ctx.exit() (which exited 0). Group.resolve_command also passes the actual remaining args instead of ctx.args when falling back to the help path for an unknown bare option. Golden tests assert exit code 2 both for a bare Command and for the no-args case of a group with arguments.
notes: No network needed at test time. Both directions plus golden tests take ~0.1s at 1 CPU. Two golden tests: test_command_no_args_is_help (renamed from the old test_no_args_is_help; the fix's version expects 2) and the parametrized test_group_with_args (5 params; only the '[]' -> exit 2 case differs from the parent's expectations). The fix touches a shared code path (parse_args on Command/Group) and adds a new exception class in exceptions.py, so a solver has to find where the exit status is produced. The 3 grep hits for `echo(ctx.get_help())` in parent core.py are the two parse_args bodies plus an unrelated spot in the main help path.
